name: Polyethylene
description: Used for less complex catheters due to its flexibility and cost-effectiveness. It is also known for its chemical resistance and biocompatibility

name: Polyurethane
description: Polyurethane's offers superior durability, strength, and flexibility, making it suitable for more intricate designs.

name: Polyvinyl chloride
description: Versatile and affordable, PVC can be formulated to be flexible, transparent, and resistant to kinks. It is a common choice, though some newer formulations are DEHP-free due to health concerns.

name: Polyether Block Amide
description: A thermoplastic elastomer family widely used in catheter shafts and distal features, valued for tunable stiffness and consistent performance in RF-based forming and joining.
long_description: PEBAX (also referred to as PEBA) is a block-copolymer thermoplastic elastomer made from polyether and polyamide segments. In catheter development, it’s frequently selected because grades span from very flexible to relatively stiff, enabling soft distal features, supportive proximal sections, and controlled transitions along the device. In RF-driven processes—such as catheter tipping, flaring, and segment-to-segment joining—PEBAX offers predictable softening and re-solidification behavior that supports repeatable geometry and smooth surface finish when heat input, alignment, and cooling are well controlled. Sterilization suitability and biocompatibility are grade- and supplier-dependent, so medical-device programs typically confirm these through supplier documentation and device-level validation.

properties.radiopacity: Often compounded with radiopaque fillers such as barium sulfate or tungsten (formulation-dependent)

applications: Catheter tipping (soft or atraumatic distal features)
Catheter flaring (expanded ends for interfaces and assemblies)
Joining catheter segments (PEBAX-to-PEBAX transitions and assemblies)
Forming smooth transitions between catheter sections

process_notes.thermal_processability: Responds well to controlled RF heating for forming and joining, supporting consistent geometry across production when the process window is dialed in.
process_notes.bonding_behavior: Typically joins well to itself; joining to dissimilar polymers is application-dependent and may require a compatible intermediate layer or surface preparation.
process_notes.tooling_considerations: Some grades can become tacky during forming; development often focuses on heat input, dwell, release strategy, and cooling to prevent sticking and maintain concentricity.

biocompatibility.usage_scope: PEBAX is offered in medical-grade formulations by major suppliers. Biocompatibility and regulatory suitability depend on the specific grade, additives, and supplier documentation, and should be confirmed as part of the device’s validation plan.

name: Thermoplastic Polyurethane
description: TPU provides excellent flexibility, abrasion resistance, and elasticity. It is ideal for catheters requiring soft, kink-resistant tubing while maintaining good mechanical strength.

name: Thermoplastic Elastomer
description: Blends the elasticity of rubber with the strength of plastic, allowing for high flexibility without kinking.

name: Polytetrafluoroethylene
description: Primarily used as an inner liner for guide catheters to provide a low-friction surface for smooth navigation.

name: Fluorinated Ethylene Propylene
description: Acts as a component to add strength or provide a heat-shrinkable covering in multi-layer catheters. Softer than PTFE and melts at a lower temperature, making it suitable for heat shrinking and other processes. It is also more translucent than PTFE.

name: Polyamide (Nylon)
description: A strong, semi-rigid polymer commonly used in catheter shafts and heat-formed tips. Polyamide offers excellent tensile strength, good kink resistance, smooth surfaces, and precise thermal-forming behavior, making it suitable for tip forming and tapering applications.

name: Polyimide
description: A high-performance, rigid polymer used in thin-wall tubing for catheter shafts. Polyimide provides exceptional tensile strength, high heat resistance, precise dimensional stability, and extremely smooth internal diameters, making it ideal for micro-catheters, hypotubes, and reinforcement layers.

name: Polypropylene
description: A lightweight, semi-rigid polymer with good chemical resistance. It is often used in less critical catheter components or connectors due to its rigidity and low cost.

name: High-Density Polyethylene
description: HDPE offers rigidity and high chemical resistance, making it suitable for structural or semi-rigid components in catheter assemblies.

name: Ethylene Tetrafluoroethylene
description: ETFE combines high mechanical strength, abrasion resistance, and chemical stability, often used as a liner or jacket for catheters requiring durability and biocompatibility.

name: Low-Density Polyethylene
description: LDPE is softer and more flexible than HDPE, making it useful for applications where gentle flexibility is desired without sacrificing chemical resistance.

name: Polyether Ether Ketone
description: PEEK is a high-performance polymer offering exceptional strength, stiffness, and temperature resistance. It is used in demanding catheter components where precision and durability are critical.
